title: A look at CloudFlare’s AI-coded OAuth library
summary: An OAuth expert reviews Cloudflare's Claude-written OAuth library: decent structure but thin tests, spec bugs and biased token generation, showing how much expertise reviewing LLM output needs.

assertions.quote: What this interaction shows is how much knowledge you need to bring when you interact with an LLM.
the code that generates token IDs is not sound: it generates biased output
there were 21 commits directly to main on the first day from one developer, no sign of any code review at all
they are woefully inadequate for what I would expect of a critical auth service

verdicts.note: Generated tests often favor happy paths unless prompted, but this depends heavily on the prompt and the reviewer.

assertions.quote: Many of these same mistakes can be found in popular Stack Overflow answers, which is probably where Claude learnt them from too.

verdicts.note: Studies of generated code show it reproduces insecure patterns common in public code, though attributing a specific bug to its source is speculative.

assertions.quote: for important things, like my fucking auth system, I’d much rather do it myself
